subject.title: [Feature]: bearer token authentication for proxy servers

question: Should OpenClaw support first-party mobile reverse-proxy transport authentication, and if so which credential types and platform surfaces are in the first supported slice?
rationale: The implementation direction changes mobile credential storage and pre-Gateway authentication behavior across setup-code, Android, iOS, and possible OIDC flows, which requires maintainer product and security intent before automation should build it.

options.title: Stage static headers first
options.body: Approve a narrow TLS-only Basic/Bearer or fixed-header contract for setup/manual mobile connections, with credential lifecycle rules and real proxy proof before merging platform slices.

options.title: Limit to the iOS Basic PR
options.body: Treat the current iOS Basic-auth PR as the only near-term scope and keep Android, bearer, custom headers, cookies, and OIDC as separate follow-up decisions.

options.title: Defer mobile proxy auth
options.body: Do not add first-party mobile proxy-credential storage yet; steer users to Tailscale, VPN, or direct trusted-proxy deployments until a sponsored design exists.

recommendation.title: Stage static headers first
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow TLS-only Basic/Bearer or fixed-header contract for setup/manual mobile connections, with credential lifecycle rules and real proxy proof before merging platform slices.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent mobile Gateway work makes this the strongest available routing owner for the shared setup/WebSocket contract question.
